monthly_review.summary: September shows a dramatic shift toward high-intensity, low-volume running with elevated physiological stress — pace improved slightly but at clear aerobic cost.
monthly_review.highlight: Z4 effort占比 surged from 8% in August to 46% in September — the largest proportional shift in intensity distribution across all months in the dataset, occurring alongside a 13 bpm rise in average heart rate and collapse of Z1 work.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km, 33.3 km must be run across 6 remaining sessions — averaging 5.6 km/session. However, current readiness is compromised (elevated HR, poor aerobic TE, Z1 near zero), so chasing this volume would likely deepen fatigue and impair adaptation. Recovery, not catch-up, is the correct priority.

insights.title: Z4 dominance masks aerobic erosion
insights.body: Z4 effort rose from 8% (Aug) to 46% (Sep), yet average HR increased +13 bpm and aerobic TE worsened (+0.4%), indicating diminishing returns — the body is working harder at the same relative intensity, not getting fitter.

insights.title: Cadence collapse correlates with high-Z4 load and elevated HR
insights.body: Cadence dropped 15 spm (149 → 134) as Z4 % quadrupled and avg HR spiked — notably, the 10.7 km run on 2026-09-06 had cadence of just 90 spm and aerobic TE of 5.0%, suggesting form breakdown under fatigue.

insights.title: Running economy improved slightly despite fatigue signals
insights.body: Avg efficiency improved marginally (14.12 → 14.05 ml/kg/km), but this occurs amid rising HR, falling cadence, and worsening aerobic TE — suggesting the improvement may reflect short-term pacing artifact (e.g., fewer easy runs) rather than true physiological gain.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤125 bpm, 45 min, Tuesday — no pace target, focus on breathing rhythm and cadence ≥145 spm
recommendations.reason: Restores autonomic balance and rebuilds Z1 tolerance; current Z1 is only 3% — baseline must be re-established before intensity makes sense.

recommendations.action: 20-min barefoot or minimalist walk + calf/Achilles mobility, Thursday evening — include 3×60-sec single-leg balance holds eyes closed
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time spiked to 389 ms (2026-09-01) and 385 ms (2026-08-23) — both >350 ms indicates neuromuscular fatigue; mobility + proprioception counters injury risk.

recommendations.action: Sleep hygiene check-in: aim for ≥7.5 hr sleep, with <30-min latency and ≤1 wake-up/night — track via Garmin Sleep Score for 3 nights
recommendations.reason: Sleep metrics are missing from dataset, but chronic sleep debt is the most likely driver of elevated resting HR trends and HRV suppression; this is the highest-leverage recovery lever.

risk_flags.evidence: Z4 % = 46% (vs 8% last month), avg HR +13 bpm, aerobic TE +0.4%, cadence -15 spm, Z1 near zero — classic signature of pushing intensity without adequate recovery foundation
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z4+ efforts for 7 days; reintroduce only after two consecutive days of HRV ≥ baseline and Z1 runs at HR ≤125 bpm

risk_flags.evidence: Ground contact time >385 ms on two recent runs (2026-08-23, 2026-09-01), vertical oscillation >9.2 mm (2026-09-03), and stride length volatility (65.7–101.8 m) suggest neuromuscular instability
risk_flags.action: Replace one run with mobility + balance work; avoid downhill or fast turnover drills until ground contact stabilizes <330 ms

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize parasympathetic activation through low-HR, rhythm-focused movement and restore sensorimotor control before reintroducing intensity.
